findings.title: retryCount delete clause not scoped to SMS method
findings.body: The new OR branch `retryCount > 1` has no `method: SMS` filter. This cron will therefore delete any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders, if other jobs ever increment retryCount. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the second OR branch.

findings.title: Scheduled reminders with retryCount>1 also deleted, losing cancel reference
findings.body: The retryCount condition has no `scheduled: false` filter, so it can also match reminders that were already scheduled at Twilio. A reminder can reach that state by failing once and later succeeding, since success does not reset retryCount. Deleting such a row drops its referenceId (the Twilio sid). The SMS can then no longer be cancelled when the booking is cancelled, so the attendee may still get it.

findings.title: Update in catch block can throw and abort the whole cron loop
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block is not itself guarded. If it throws (for example a DB error, or the row was removed concurrently), the exception escapes the for loop. All remaining reminders in this run are then skipped and the handler errors out.
